steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Igneous rocks form from the cooling and crystallisation of magma (intrusive) or lava (extrusive) | Key Fact: Intrusive igneous rocks cool slowly underground, producing large visible crystals (coarse-grained): granite, gabbro, diorite | Key Fact: Extrusive igneous rocks cool rapidly at the surface, producing fine-grained or glassy textures: basalt, rhyolite, andesite, obsidian | Key Fact: Granite (felsic, intrusive) = quartz + feldspar + mica; Basalt (mafic, extrusive) = pyroxene + plagioclase + olivine
